forecasts.reason: A first port of airbench96 to CIFAR-100 at 9 epochs with no TTA is plausibly near the 0.753 bar but likely misses it; the port has many untuned details and a bug risk.
A half-epoch change moves accuracy about 0.3 pp, comparable to the 3-seed noise (about 0.2 pp), so the slope is hard to read and the sign is likely but the size is uncertain.
Compile and fused SGD likely give a 5-15% speedup with the same accuracy, but max-autotune can cause recompiles or eval shape problems that eat the gain.
Lookahead gain at 9 epochs is expected to be about 0.1-0.3 pp, which is within noise, so a clean support is not likely.
Identical reruns should have time within 2% and per-seed accuracy std around 0.2-0.4 pp, so the noise hypothesis is likely to hold.
Dropping the ragged batch saves little if build already warmed it up, so the 0.3 s claim is uncertain, and dropping data changes accuracy slightly.
Muon from an untuned start with a bf16 Newton-Schulz step adds overhead, and the epoch savings are unlikely to appear without tuning.
Progressive resizing at low epoch counts usually costs more than 0.2 pp, and the time saved is eaten by extra warmup and interpolate overhead.

cruxes: Does the first airbench96-style port at 9 epochs reach 0.753 on CIFAR-100, or does it need 11-14 epochs?
What is the per-seed accuracy std and the run-to-run time noise?
How much of the wall time is fixed cost (prepare, data transfer, compile leakage) versus per-epoch cost?
